title: bug: moe-proxy exits before a one-shot reply over 64 KiB is fully written on Linux/macOS/WSL, so wrapper RPCs read a truncated JSON line
description:
Files: packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts, plus a test under packages/moe-proxy/src/ (index.test.ts or a new file). No open row declares any moe-proxy file. I checked the plan files of every non-DONE row at 2026-11-02 20:51Z, so this row is off the wrapper lanes.

Defect, read at HEAD 3e092cff:
- Every reply goes out through safeStdoutWrite (index.ts:186-199), a bare process.stdout.write with no completion callback. The ws 'message' handler writes the daemon's reply at :570.
- A one-shot call (`echo "$rpc" | node dist/index.js`) hits stdin EOF at once. gracefulShutdown exits immediately when nothing is pending (:368-370). Otherwise drainTick runs every 50 ms and calls process.exit(0) as soon as the reply's id leaves pendingRequestIds (:415-419).
- On POSIX, Node writes to a pipe asynchronously. The kernel takes about 64 KiB, libuv queues the rest, and process.exit() does not wait for that queue, so the tail is dropped. Windows stdout pipes are synchronous, so the ps1 path should be unaffected; that is not tested.
- Measured in this WSL checkout with Node v24.21.0, using a standalone script that copies the proxy's write-then-exit timing: a 300 KB line arrived as 131,072 bytes in 2 of 5 runs. Through bash `$(...)` at the proxy's 50 ms tick, the line was cut in 3/30 runs at 100 KB, 6/30 at 1 MB and 9/30 at 3 MB.

Reach:
- Every bash-wrapper one-shot RPC whose reply passes about 64 KiB: scripts/moe-agent.sh moe_rpc and scripts/moe-call.sh. That covers the pre-flight get_context preload, claims of large tasks, post-flight and adoption reads, and list/log reads.
- The daemon has already executed the call, but the wrapper sees a JSON parse failure: moe_rpc returns 1, and moe-call.sh exits 1.
- Most of the fleet runs bash seats under WSL. A failed pre-flight get_context read is the trigger of in-flight task-31187ec1, so this bug makes that path fire more often.

Origin: hunt requested by governor-e6b40560 (msg-5fe3b1537cb04b50964bd0edf07db4c8). task-35584de2 [CQ-C00] fixed the same write-then-exit pattern in moe-call.sh's own Node parser, and that row put proxy changes explicitly out of scope.

Fix direction (decided at planning): route the two success exits (:370 and :419) through one helper that exits only after stdout has drained, e.g. `process.stdout.write('', () => process.exit(code))`, with an unref'd guard timer for a reader that never drains. The EPIPE exit(1) path stays as it is.
definitionOfDone: A one-shot run with stdin at EOF and stdout piped delivers a reply of at least 2 MB complete: the line parses as JSON and its byte length equals what the fake daemon sent. This holds on both success-exit paths: gracefulShutdown's immediate exit when nothing is pending, and drainTick's exit after the last reply.

A new test under packages/moe-proxy/src drives the real proxy entry against a fake daemon. Its reader waits at least 200 ms before draining stdout, so the unchanged proxy truncates every time on POSIX. RED first: the test fails against the unchanged index.ts, and the completion evidence quotes the failure.

A reader that never drains cannot keep the proxy alive more than 5 s after the reply. The EPIPE exit(1) path, the MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS bound, and the existing EOF grace and drain cases in index.test.ts and input-framing.test.ts behave exactly as before.

`cd packages/moe-proxy && npx vitest run` exits 0. Run it in the task's worktree or in a git-archive snapshot, never through `npm run build` in the shared control checkout. Its output is the complete_task evidence.
Only files under packages/moe-proxy/ change: src/index.ts, its tests, and README.md's one-shot section if the exit wording changes.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (RED). Create packages/moe-proxy/src/stdout-drain.test.ts with the Write tool (global rule [2]). Do not edit index.test.ts or input-framing.test.ts: DoD 3 needs their EOF grace and drain cases unchanged. First read mem:gotcha-proxy-test-harness (cleanup shape), mem:gotcha-proxy-tests-compile-into-dist-es2022 (npm run build type-checks this file under strict ES2022: no findLast/toSorted) and /mnt/d/moe-scratch/65ab45fe-plan/README.md. That README is the architect's prototype: prototype-harness.mjs drove the HEAD build and the patched build through these same 4 cases, 5 runs each.

Wrap everything in describe.skipIf(process.platform === 'win32'), with a comment: Node makes a Windows stdout pipe blocking, so the write itself waits for the reader and no queued tail can be lost. (A reader that never drains then blocks the proxy inside the write, which is out of scope.)

Harness, shaped like index.test.ts:
- A temp project dir whose .moe/daemon.json {port, pid, startedAt, projectPath} points at new WebSocketServer({ port: 0 }) (await 'listening').
- Fake daemon: count connections. On each message, after delayMs, send ONE reply JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: msg.id, result: { content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'x'.repeat(2 * 1024 * 1024) }] } }) and record sentAt and sentBytes = Buffer.byteLength(reply). Record closedAt on that ws's 'close'.
- Spawn process.execPath on path.join(__dirname, '../dist/index.js') with env { ...process.env, MOE_PROJECT_PATH: testDir }. vitest.config.ts already blanks the seat's MOE_* vars; an inherited MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.x would send the proxy to the Windows host. Collect stderr as text.

The reader is the crux. Register the collector AT SPAWN and pause it at once: proxy.stdout.on('data', (c) => chunks.push(c)); proxy.stdout.pause(); const ended = once(proxy.stdout, 'end'). Never attach it later: when a child exits, Node's child_process resumes an unconsumed stdout and discards it (flushStdio), so a late reader makes the RED run hang instead of fail.
- Reader gate: wait (bounded 10 s) until the fake daemon has seen the proxy close its socket (closedAt set; closeWebSocket() runs just before either exit) AND Date.now() - sentAt >= 300 (DoD 2 asks for at least 200 ms). Then resume() and await 'end', bounded.
- Every wait is bounded and clears its timer on both paths.
- afterEach SIGKILLs a still-running child, terminates the server's clients, closes the server, and runs rmSync(testDir, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 5 }).

Cases. Assert numbers before parsing, and never diff the 2 MB string, so the RED output quotes cleanly:
(1) drainTick exit: wait for a connection, write one tools/call line (moe.list_tasks, id 1) and end stdin at once. The daemon replies after 100 ms, so the id is still pending at EOF. After the gate: exactly one '\n'-terminated line; expect(Buffer.byteLength(line)).toBe(sentBytes); JSON.parse(line) has id 1 and result.content[0].text.length 2 * 1024 * 1024; exit code 0.
(2) gracefulShutdown immediate exit: write the request but keep stdin open; the daemon replies at once. Wait until proxy.stdout.readableLength > 0: the reply is written and its id forgotten, so nothing is pending. Then end stdin. Same gate and assertions as (1).
(3) Never-drain guard: as (1), but never resume. Await exit (bounded 10 s): code 1, exitAt - sentAt >= 1800 and < 5000 (DoD 3's 5 s bound), and stderr matches /stdout did not drain within 2000ms/.
(4) EPIPE: as (1) up to the gate, then proxy.stdout.destroy() instead of reading. Expect exit code 1 within 1000 ms of the destroy, well inside the 2 s guard, which proves it is the EPIPE path, and stderr matching /stdout write failed: .*EPIPE/.

RED run (DoD 2), with index.ts still unchanged. Run it in a snapshot only (mem:gotcha-proxy-npm-test-shared-checkout-deletes-dist), from WSL bash:
R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel) && S=$(mktemp -d) && git -C "$R" archive HEAD | tar -x -C "$S" && cp "$R/packages/moe-proxy/src/stdout-drain.test.ts" "$S/packages/moe-proxy/src/" && cd "$S/packages/moe-proxy" && npm ci && npm run build && npx vitest run src/stdout-drain.test.ts
Expected: all 4 cases fail on Linux. (1) and (2) fail on byte counts: the prototype saw 146,176 or 182,720 bytes against 2,097,225. (3) and (4) fail with exit code 0 where 1 is expected. If a case passes, the test is wrong: fix the test, never the thresholds. Keep the failure lines for the complete_task summary. Error handling: if vitest stops with 'Cannot find native binding', see mem:gotcha-gate-snapshot-psparse-and-proxy-rolldown.
implementationPlan.note: RED against unchanged index.ts (snapshot of HEAD, npm ci + build + vitest run src/stdout-drain.test.ts): 4/4 fail. (1) drainTick: expected 146176 to be 2097225 (line bytes). (2) gracefulShutdown immediate: expected 146176 to be 2097225. (3) never-drain: expected +0 to be 1 (exit code). (4) EPIPE: expected +0 to be 1 (exit code). Reader is registered at spawn and paused; gate = fake daemon saw socket close AND >=300ms since send. Cases 1/2 also assert the exit path via stderr ('Waiting for 1 pending request' present for drainTick, absent for immediate).

Added STDOUT_DRAIN_GUARD_MS (2000) and exitAfterStdoutDrain() next to safeStdoutWrite; replaced only the two success exits (gracefulShutdown nothing-pending branch, drainTick tail), closeWebSocket() still first in both; updated gracefulShutdown's doc comment. Snapshot run (build + vitest run src/stdout-drain.test.ts): 4/4 pass, 3 consecutive runs. tsc build/type-check clean.

implementationPlan.description:
DOCS. Edit packages/moe-proxy/README.md only, in its '## One-shot calls' section. DoD 5 allows this edit because the exit wording changes.

After the paragraph that ends 'cap any drain at 2 seconds.', add one paragraph of 2-3 sentences:
- The proxy exits 0 only after its stdout has drained, so a reader that starts late still gets all of a reply bigger than the OS pipe buffer (about 64 KiB on Linux).
- A reader that stops reading gets 2 seconds; then the proxy exits 1, because the reply may be incomplete.
- A reader that closes the pipe (EPIPE) gets exit 1, as before.

Touch nothing else. The deadline paragraph stays true as written.
implementationPlan.note: Added one 3-sentence paragraph to '## One-shot calls' after the paragraph ending 'cap any drain at 2 seconds.'; nothing else touched.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, the final step. Load the adversarial-self-review skill and read your own diff of the 3 files as an attacker. Check:
- Twice or concurrently: the two exits are mutually exclusive and each runs at most once. If the guard and the callback both fire, the first exit wins.
- An EPIPE during the wait exits 1, never 0.
- A SIGTERM/SIGINT during the wait: gracefulShutdown returns early (shuttingDown), and the 2 s guard bounds it.
- MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS during the wait: expireDeadline is unchanged, and it still exits 1.
- Small replies gain no delay: the callback runs on the next tick, so 'exits immediately when no pending requests' (<500 ms) stays green.
- Nothing new writes to stdout during the wait. stdin is at EOF, the timeout checker and drain timer are stopped, and the daemon sends no unsolicited /mcp notifications (server/WebSocketServer.ts, McpAdapter.ts).
- Windows: pipes are synchronous, so behavior there is unchanged.
- Tests: every wait is bounded, nothing leaks a child or server on failure, failure output never prints the 2 MB string, and only win32 skips.
- The forbidden-pattern rails, and ES2022 APIs only.
- Scope is exactly 3 files, about +230 net LOC, under the 400 cap.

Fix what you find, re-run step 4's exact command if any code changed, then call complete_task.
implementationPlan.note: Self-review of the 3-file diff, no code change needed (so step 4's gate result stands). Checked: (1) the helper runs at most once per path; gracefulShutdown returns early on shuttingDown and drainTick clears its interval first; the immediate branch never arms drainTimer; process.exit is synchronous, so guard-vs-callback first-wins. (2) EPIPE: the callback gets err before the 'error' event and exits 1 (case 4 proves it). (3) SIGTERM/SIGINT during the wait: gracefulShutdown no-ops, the 2s guard bounds it. (4) Late/duplicate daemon replies during the wait are dropped by the ws 'message' handler (id no longer pending); ws 'close'/'error' on the nulled socket take the stale-socket early return, so no reconnect or stdout write. (5) Small replies: empty-write callback on next tick, existing 'exits immediately' test green. (6) Theoretical, left as documented in the plan: expireDeadline firing inside the <=2s flush window still exits 1 as before, and with no pending ids it also writes its null-id error line after a possibly partial reply; the exit code is still 1, so moe_rpc fails. (7) Theoretical: a signal during the wait leaves stdin attached for up to 2s, same as the existing drain path. (8) Tests: every wait bounded and its timer cleared; cleanups registered before any await and drained in reverse; failure output carries only numbers, never the 2 MB string; only win32 skips; no forbidden patterns, no ES2023 APIs. Scope: 3 files, +35/-3 index.ts, +2 README, 257-line new test (about 294 net, under the 400 cap).

reopenReason: Human "move from backlog"; architect hunt row, confirmed at 3e092cff: proxy one-shot stdout truncation >64 KiB on POSIX. HIGH.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: On stdin EOF, moe-proxy's two success exits wait until stdout has drained to the OS before exiting 0: gracefulShutdown when nothing is pending, and drainTick after the last reply. A one-shot reply bigger than the ~64 KiB pipe buffer then arrives complete on POSIX even when the reader starts late. An EPIPE during the wait exits 1. A reader that never drains is cut off 2 s later with exit 1. JSON-RPC output bytes are unchanged; only exit timing changes.
acceptanceCriteria: The new stdout-drain.test.ts cases (1) drainTick exit and (2) gracefulShutdown immediate exit each deliver one line whose byte length equals the fake daemon's 2 MB reply, which parses as JSON, with exit 0.
Case (3): a never-read stdout makes the proxy exit 1, at least 1.8 s and less than 5 s after the reply, logging 'stdout did not drain within 2000ms'.
Case (4): destroying the reader mid-wait gives exit 1 within 1 s, logging 'stdout write failed: ... EPIPE'.
Against unchanged index.ts, all 4 new cases fail on Linux, and the completion summary quotes that failure.
invariants: safeStdoutWrite, main()'s stdout 'error' handler, expireDeadline and every process.exit(1) path are unchanged.
closeWebSocket() still runs before the exit wait.
index.test.ts, input-framing.test.ts and vitest.config.ts are not edited.
No npm ci/build/test runs in the shared checkout; tracked files are written only with Edit/Write.
compatibility: No MCP/JSON-RPC wire change: every byte forwarded to stdout is unchanged.
Windows stdout pipes are synchronous (Node sets them blocking), so the ps1 path behaves exactly as before.
The interactive CLI sessions take the same exit path; a CLI that stopped reading costs at most 2 s.
approvedScope: packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts: new const STDOUT_DRAIN_GUARD_MS and function exitAfterStdoutDrain(); gracefulShutdown's nothing-pending branch and drainTick's tail call it instead of process.exit(0).
packages/moe-proxy/README.md '## One-shot calls': one added paragraph.
reuse: Node's own Writable callback ordering (an empty write's callback runs after earlier writes flush); no new dependency or internal API.
CQ-C00 (35cf53c8) fixed moe-call.sh's parser with process.exitCode and a natural exit. That does not work here: ws's 30 s close timer and the deadline timer keep the loop alive.
sourceAssumptions: packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts gracefulShutdown: closeWebSocket(); process.exit(0) when pendingRequestIds and pendingMessages are empty (HEAD 96c4ee19 lines 368-371).
packages/moe-proxy/src/index.ts safeStdoutWrite (186-199) is a bare process.stdout.write with no callback; the ws 'message' handler writes replies through it (570).
scripts/moe-agent.sh moe_rpc: raw=$(echo "$rpc" | node proxy) || return 1, so a non-zero proxy exit already fails the RPC.
The daemon sends no unsolicited notifications on /mcp (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts, McpAdapter.ts).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) process.exitCode and a natural exit, as CQ-C00 did in moe-call.sh: rejected. ws's 30 s close-handshake timer and an armed MOE_PROXY_ONESHOT_DEADLINE_MS timer hold the loop open. (b) Waiting on 'drain' and polling writableLength: more code, same effect. (c) Making stdout blocking via _handle.setBlocking: rejected. It is an internal API, blocks the event loop, and hangs forever on a reader that never drains. (d) Guard exit 0: rejected. The reply may be incomplete, and exit 1 makes moe_rpc fail honestly instead of on a JSON parse error. Chosen: an empty process.stdout.write callback plus an unref'd 2 s guard, the decided direction.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Measured by the architect on Linux WSL2, node v24.21.0, artifacts in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/65ab45fe-plan:
- A plain exit after a 2 MB write delivers 65,536 bytes to a reader that sleeps 300 ms. Through the real proxy with a paused child_process reader it delivers 146,176 or 182,720 bytes, deterministically, both exit paths, 5/5 runs.
- The patched build delivers 2,097,225 of 2,097,225 bytes, 5/5. Never-drain exits 1 at 2,053-2,055 ms. EPIPE exits 1 7-11 ms after the reader closes.
- Test pitfall: Node's child_process flushStdio resumes and discards an unconsumed child stdout when the child exits, so a reader that attaches late sees no 'end'. Register the collector at spawn and pause() it.
- Prototype gotcha: an inherited MOE_DAEMON_HOST=172.x sends a spawned proxy to the Windows host. vitest.config.ts already blanks it.
- The full proxy suite needs packages/moe-daemon npm ci (workerType.integration.test.ts) and packages/moe-claude-plugin/package.json (buildScriptOrder.test.ts), hence a whole-HEAD archive.
- No proxy or daemon-server change between claim HEAD 3e092cff and 96c4ee19.
planningNotes.risks:
- A deadline that expires during the <=2 s flush wait still exits 1 at once, leaving expireDeadline unchanged and truncating the tail. That is the documented whole-process bound.
- A signal during the wait is bounded by the guard.
- macOS pipes start at 16 KiB but are async, like Linux.
- Windows is skipped on purpose; CI runs the proxy suite on ubuntu only.
- Timing margins are wide (gate at 300 ms vs a 2 s guard; never-drain exits at about 2.05 s vs a 5 s bound), but vitest runs files in parallel on a busy shared host: keep the thresholds, and fix flaky waits rather than loosening the asserts.
- Fleet impact needs the governor to stage and swap a rebuilt packages/moe-proxy/dist. A landed src fix alone changes nothing live.
